candidates.label: Primary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the central nervous system (PCNSL)
missing_or_uncertain: Absence of contrast enhancement on MRI is atypical but not exclusionary
No evidence of systemic disease outside CNS

candidates.label: Secondary CNS involvement by systemic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (with occult systemic disease)
missing_or_uncertain: Bone marrow negative but other extranodal sites not evaluated

candidates.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, low-grade B-cell type (e.g., marginal zone lymphoma)
missing_or_uncertain: Markers (CD19+, CD20+, BCL6+, MUM-1+) are more typical of high-grade DLBCL
FISH shows extra copies of BCL6 and BCL2, often seen in aggressive lymphomas

candidates.label: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (double-hit lymphoma)
missing_or_uncertain: FISH shows extra copies, not rearrangements; double-hit requires MYC rearrangement

candidates.label: Glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) with reactive lymphoid infiltrate
missing_or_uncertain: Biopsy shows clonal B-cell population, not reactive
CSF lymphoma cells confirm leptomeningeal involvement

response.rationale: The biopsy showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ cells and CSF lymphoma cells are diagnostic of a B-cell lymphoma. The absence of bone marrow involvement and lack of systemic symptoms favor primary CNS lymphoma over secondary. The lack of contrast enhancement is atypical but does not exclude PCNSL. Other differentials are far less likely given the definitive biopsy and cytogenetic findings.
